entries.meaning: I revere Rāma: worshipped by Śiva, the enemy of Kāma; remover of the fear of worldly existence and a lion to the maddened elephant of Time; lord of yogins, reached through knowledge, an unconquered treasury of virtues, beyond attributes and change; beyond māyā, lord of the gods, intent upon destroying the wicked and the one deity of the Brahmin host; dark and beautiful as a rain-bearing cloud, lotus-eyed, the divine one in the form of an earthly king.
entries.note: Original close English rendering from the pinned Devanagari witness; editorial work awaiting independent review. Kandāvadātam follows the contextual Manas reading of a beautiful rain-bearing cloud; its lexical formation remains a point for specialist review.

entries.meaning: I bow to the worshipful Śaṅkara, husband of Girijā, treasury of virtues and destroyer of Kāma: his exceedingly beautiful body gleams like conch and moon, tiger-hide is his garment, the fearsome serpent of Time is worn as a formidable ornament, and Gaṅgā and the moon are dear to him. He is lord of Kāśī, stiller of the flood of Kali's impurities, and the wish-fulfilling tree of well-being.

entries.meaning: May that Śaṅkara—Śambhu, who grants the good even the rare state of absolute liberation, and who punishes the wicked—extend auspiciousness to me.
entries.note: Original close English rendering of the pinned edition-specific final reading mām; editorial work awaiting independent review.

entries.meaning: Instants, twinklings, atoms of time, ages, years and aeons are his fierce arrows. O mind, why do you not worship that Rāma, whose bow is Time itself?
entries.note: Original close English rendering of the pinned Awadhi reading; editorial work awaiting independent review.

entries.meaning: After hearing the ocean's words, Rāma summoned his counsellors and the Lord spoke thus: ‘What purpose does delay serve now? Build the bridge so that the army may cross.’
entries.note: Original close English rendering of the pinned Awadhi reading; editorial work awaiting independent review.

entries.meaning: Jāmbavān joined his hands and said, ‘Listen, O banner of the solar lineage: Lord, your name is the bridge; by mounting it, human beings will cross the ocean of worldly existence.’
